extracted: US National Vital Statistics System mortality files, 2017–2023, US residents who died in the US: an overdose death has an ICD-10 underlying cause of X40–X44 (unintentional), X60–X64 (suicide), X85 (homicide) or Y10–Y14 (undetermined intent), which reflect acute intoxication; deaths from chronic drug exposure (such as liver toxicity) and adverse effects of therapeutic or prophylactic doses are excluded. The literal text is written by the medical certifier, usually a medical examiner or coroner for overdose deaths; NCHS software searches Part I, Part II and the how-the-injury-occurred field, and a mentioned drug is assumed to be involved unless the surrounding words say otherwise. ICD-10 drug codes are broad: fentanyl, Demerol, tramadol, nitazenes and Suboxone all fall under T40.4, and oxycodone under T40.2 with drugs such as codeine and morphine.

extracted: Coroners or medical examiners determine the cause of death and complete the certificate; NCHS codes the text to ICD-10 with software that automates the coding. Naming an opioid analgesic (for example hydrocodone, methadone or tramadol) gives a code in T40.2–T40.4; writing 'opioid' alone gives T40.6 (other and unspecified narcotics); writing simply 'drug overdose' gives T50.9 (other and unspecified drugs), and the opioid's contribution disappears from the coded data.
